article.headline: A Gallery That Documents What Browsers Can Actually Render
article.lede: mesh3d.gallery is a hand-curated showcase of 258 websites, all built with real-time WebGL or Three.js, all selected on a single editorial test: does it prove what a browser can genuinely render? Launched in early 2026 by two Bratislava-based builders, it is simultaneously an archive of the creative web at its most technically demanding and an argument that this kind of ambition should be the norm, not the exception.
article.body:
mesh3d.gallery was built by Andrej Bronček, a product owner at Bratislava-based invoicing firm Sufio by day, and his co-founder Majo Puterka, a product designer. Their curatorial rule is strict: only sites that render genuine real-time 3D geometry qualify; pre-rendered video dressed up as interactivity is out. When the founders announced on Hacker News in April 2026, they framed it plainly — they wanted one place to prove what a browser can actually do. The gallery now holds 258 entries, split between finished commercial work and 42 standalone experiments, giving it the feel of a gallery with a sketchbook annex.

The enabling technology is mostly *Three.js*, a JavaScript library that wraps the raw **WebGL** graphics API in a developer-friendly interface. WebGL, standardized by the Khronos Group in 2011, lets a browser talk directly to a device's GPU — no plugin required. Three.js, first released in 2010 by Ricardo Cabello (known online as “mrdoob”), logs 2.7 million npm downloads per week and carries over 112,000 GitHub stars. The next step in the stack is *WebGPU* — a more efficient successor that more closely mirrors how modern GPUs work — which became cross-browser in 2025 when Safari 26 completed support. The gallery's technology map is, in effect, a portrait of the open web's rendering ambition across fifteen years.

The most-represented studios show what this craft looks like at commercial scale. Lusion (14 entries), a Bristol outfit founded in 2017 by self-taught technologist Edan Kwan, has built interactive work for Coca-Cola (KO), Apple (AAPL), and Google (GOOGL) while collecting 58 Awwwards — the web-design industry's most coveted peer recognition. Unseen Studio (23 entries), a brand and motion studio formerly named Green Chameleon, holds the highest entry count in the gallery; PeachWeb (16 entries) takes the opposite angle, billing itself as the world's first no-code 3D website builder, democratizing what everyone else in the gallery builds by hand.

The timing reflects a genuine convergence. Platform conditioning from TikTok and Instagram has reset user expectations for visual richness in ways that now spill onto the open web; WebGL 2.0 is universal, Three.js is mature, and AI tools have lowered the floor for *creative coding* — the practice of writing software primarily for aesthetic or expressive ends rather than functional ones. The global immersive content creation market was estimated at $15.7 billion in 2024 and projected to reach $56.3 billion by 2030. mesh3d.gallery sits at the craft end of that curve, documenting the studios and independent developers proving what the medium can do before the broader market catches up.

One entry worth noting is the site for *Launch It*, a 2016 career handbook by creative director Shane Mielke — whose résumé includes design work for SpaceX's Crew Dragon spacecraft interfaces and an Emmy, shared with the NASA/SpaceX broadcast team, for the first crewed Dragon flight. The book is a guide for digital creatives; the website is itself a WebGL experience. That the gallery includes it as both captures something essential about the community it serves: people for whom the line between tool and artwork is genuinely blurred.

concepts.definition: A web standard maintained by the Khronos Group that gives JavaScript programs direct access to a device's graphics processing unit (GPU) through the browser. First released in 2011, it enables hardware-accelerated 3D graphics without plugins — the same GPU that renders video games can render a webpage in real time.

An open-source JavaScript library that makes writing 3D graphics for the browser dramatically easier by providing a high-level API on top of raw WebGL. Created by Ricardo Cabello in 2010, it is the dominant tool in the creative web space, with 2.7 million npm downloads per week and over 112,000 GitHub stars.

The next-generation browser graphics standard, developed by the W3C with contributions from Apple, Google, and Mozilla. It offers lower overhead and better performance than WebGL by more closely mirroring how modern GPUs actually work. Cross-browser support arrived in 2025 when Safari 26 added it, completing coverage across all major browsers.

The practice of writing software whose primary goal is aesthetic, expressive, or experimental rather than purely functional. It encompasses generative art, interactive browser experiences, and data visualization as art — the kind of work mesh3d.gallery curates.

A competitive recognition platform for web design and development that distributes awards including Site of the Day, Site of the Year, and Design Studio of the Year. It is the most widely cited prestige signal in the professional web-design industry, with awards actively influencing studio reputations and client acquisition.

Graphics computed and displayed on-the-fly by the user's own hardware, as opposed to pre-calculated sequences played back as video. It enables genuine interactivity — the scene responds to mouse movement, scroll position, or physics — and is the core criterion mesh3d.gallery uses to select entries.

The default package registry for the JavaScript ecosystem, where developers publish and download reusable code libraries. Weekly download counts on npm serve as a standard proxy for how widely a library is actually being used in production projects across the industry.

books.title: Launch It
books.author: Shane Mielke
books.summary: A 2016 handbook for digital creatives by Creative Director Shane Mielke, distilling ten years of agency life — at 2Advanced Studios and with clients including Disney, NASA, and Blizzard Entertainment — into practical advice on process, career navigation, freelance, and work ethic. Unusually, the promotional website for the book is itself a WebGL experience, making it both a guide to the creative-web community and a specimen of it.

repos.summary: Three.js is the dominant JavaScript library for 3D graphics in the browser, providing a high-level API over raw WebGL. With over 112,000 GitHub stars and 2.7 million weekly npm downloads — roughly 270 times more than the next major alternative — it is the primary enabling technology behind the majority of entries on mesh3d.gallery. Since release r171 in September 2025, an experimental WebGPU renderer is included with zero additional configuration.

ticker_aapl.name: Apple Inc.
ticker_aapl.blurb: Apple designs and markets consumer electronics (iPhone, Mac, iPad, Apple Watch), software, and digital services. The iPhone remains the dominant revenue driver, but the Services segment — comprising the App Store, Apple Music, iCloud, Apple Pay, and licensing — has grown into a high-margin business that Wall Street values separately. Apple commands one of the highest brand loyalty rates in consumer technology and operates a tightly integrated hardware-software ecosystem.
ticker_aapl.recent: Apple reported FY2025 revenue of approximately $400 billion. The company has faced headwinds from slowing iPhone upgrade cycles in mature markets and regulatory pressure on App Store commissions in both the US and EU. Apple Intelligence, its generative AI suite, launched in late 2024 but has not yet materially re-accelerated upgrade cycles. Paul Pelosi sold 45,000 shares of AAPL according to the January 2026 PTR disclosure — the largest single sale in the filing by share count.

ticker_googl.name: Alphabet Inc. (Class A)
ticker_googl.blurb: Alphabet is the parent company of Google, the world's dominant search engine, as well as YouTube, the Google Cloud Platform, and a portfolio of moonshot bets (Waymo, DeepMind, Verily). Search advertising accounts for the majority of revenue, but the cloud division has grown into a multi-billion-dollar profit centre. Alphabet is also a leading player in generative AI, having developed the Gemini family of large language models and integrated them across its product suite.
ticker_googl.recent: Alphabet reported FY2025 revenue of approximately $370 billion, with Google Cloud crossing $50 billion annually. The company has faced antitrust scrutiny in both the US and EU, with a US federal court ruling in 2024 that Google holds an illegal monopoly in general search. Despite regulatory headwinds, the stock has benefited from AI-driven search enhancements and strong cloud growth. Paul Pelosi exercised call options with a $150 strike (purchased January 2025, exercised January 2026) gaining approximately 75% over the period.
